title: Ambiguous `length` Unit (Bytes vs Characters vs Words)
pattern: A parameter or field named `length` or `size` representing string or buffer boundaries without specifying the unit of measurement.
why_bad: In multi-byte string encodings (like UTF-8 in Rust), `length` is ambiguous. It could mean bytes, characters, or words. Slicing a Rust `&str` by character count using byte indices causes runtime panics or corrupts unicode boundaries.
detection: Match functions taking `&str` or `String` and a parameter named `length`, `size`, or `limit` of a numeric type.
source: *The Art of Readable Code* by Dustin Boswell and Trevor Foucher (Chapter 3, p. 24).
